question: What maximum inbound QQ gateway frame size should the bundled QQBot client enforce without rejecting supported events?
rationale: The available evidence establishes the need for a memory bound but not the QQ protocol's maximum valid server frame, so automation cannot safely choose the delivery-versus-availability boundary.

options.title: Use a contract-backed ceiling
options.body: Adopt the official QQ maximum with measured headroom and test both rejection and reconnect behavior.

options.title: Approve a measured conservative ceiling
options.body: If QQ publishes no maximum, have the QQBot owner approve a value backed by representative live event sizes and redacted runtime proof.

options.title: Retain the ws default
options.body: Close the PR and accept the current 100 MiB library ceiling until a defensible QQ-specific boundary is available.

recommendation.title: Use a contract-backed ceiling
recommendation.body: Adopt the official QQ maximum with measured headroom and test both rejection and reconnect behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged QQBot gateway architecture work is the strongest ownership signal for this transport boundary.
